title: Sindri, agent-first
headline: Say it in one sentence to an agent,
headline_em: and the workflow exists and runs.
lede: Sindri drops recipes, the factory pipeline and approvals. In their place: workflows as graphs of generic blocks, built over MCP, plus connections, memory, toolkits and resources an agent can set up without anyone opening the app.
notes: Four parts: why, how a workflow is built and run, the platform pieces around it, and the build plan. The ask at the end is to confirm the phase order.

sections.title: Small automations are impossible to build today
sections.lede: The everyday work that keeps a team moving is trigger → agent → condition → notify. Sindri can't express it without new code.

pains.title: Blocks know their station
pains.text: `step.scope.*`, `step.lens.round` and the line dispatcher only make sense inside the one pipeline, so nothing is reusable.

pains.title: Every change waits for a human
pains.text: Profile edits, recipes and pins sit until `sindri profile approve <hash>` is typed in a human terminal.

pains.title: Agents are locked out
pains.text: Agent sessions are refused at 89 call sites, so an agent can't build or run what it was asked to.

pains.title: The pipeline never worked
pains.text: Intake → scoping → design → build → prove → ship was too ambitious to be reliable.

sections.alt: Docs and blocks, create, validate, test run, read the run, fix with apply_ops and validate again, then activate.

sections.title: The first workflow, built by an agent

steps.title: Says one sentence
steps.note: "Every weekday at 7, check whether repo B's client matches repo A's API contracts and open a PR if it drifted."
steps.html: > every weekday at 7, check whether repo B's client matches repo A's API contracts and open a PR if it drifted

steps.title: Reads the blocks and drafts four nodes
steps.note: `workflow_blocks`, then `workflow_create` with schedule → run_agent → condition → notify.
steps.html:
schedule 0 7 * * 1-5
→ run_agent repo B (A read-only)
→ condition {{agent.drifted}}
→ notify owner

steps.title: Validates and test-runs it
steps.note: `workflow_validate` returns no findings; `workflow_run` runs it now; `workflow_run_get` shows each node's output.
steps.html:
run wf_01@1:manual-1 · succeeded
agent → {drifted: false, checkedCommit: a41f0c2}

steps.title: Fix one thing together
steps.note: The owner wants the commit remembered; the agent adds `memory_write` with `workflow_apply_ops` against revision 1.
steps.html:
apply_ops base=1
+ memory_write drift-check
→ revision 2

steps.title: Activates it
steps.note: `workflow_activate` pins revision 2. The next weekday at 7 it runs on its own; a drift opens a PR and notifies the owner.
steps.html:
active: revision 2
next run: Mon 07:00

sections.title: A trigger becomes exactly one run, and long waits are Temporal waits
sections.alt: Trigger, run id, duplicate check, concurrency, GraphWorkflow walking nodes, one activity per node, waits for agent reports or answers, ledger mirror.

sections.title: A run's status only moves forward
sections.rule: run id = <workflow>@<revision>:<occurrence>; a second start with the same id is refused

sections.title: A workflow is a slug plus immutable revisions

rules.title: Revisions are immutable
rules.text: A save writes a new revision; activation pins one; a run records which one it used.

sections.title: A run and its node runs record exactly what happened
Sign in once; workflows use a connection by name, never the token
sections.alt: connection_add by kind: browser consent with PKCE and loopback for oauth or mcp, pasted key or CLI login for rest or cli; secrets in the OS keychain; refreshed before expiry; a failed refresh raises needs-sign-in; nodes name a connection and the sandbox gets the token, CLI, MCP entry and host group.

sections.title: Nothing is lost while the laptop sleeps
sections.alt: Poll service every 2 minutes and a catch-up on start or wake both read cursors per connection and event kind; events carry delivery ids; matched triggers start runs once; a missed schedule runs once.

sections.title: Outside systems hand work over through a pull inbox
sections.alt: Sindri polls an outside inbox API, claims an offer, makes an item, runs a workflow with an inbox trigger and submits its outputs; local apps can POST to the handoff endpoint.
